newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican daily port, shipping update for April 9.
newsitem.headline: Mexican daily port, shipping update for April 9.

text.p: Four Gulf of Mexico ports were shut as a sudden storm hit the Gulf of Mexico on Wednesday, the Communications and Transport Ministry (SCT) said in its 1500 local/2000 GMT daily meteorological report.
Two of Mexico's three crude ports were shut to oil exports. Pajaritos in Veracruz state was shut at 1100 local/1600 GMT and Dos Bocas in Tabasco state closed at 1245 local/1745 GMT.
Port officials told Reuters winds had been up to 65 km per hour, but had died down and the ports could open later in the day.
Cayo Arcas in Campeche state remained open to exports, with two ships loading crude, a port official told Reuters.
Ciudad del Carmen and Campeche ports were also closed, the report said.
The ministry updated port conditions and shipping warnings for the Pacific Coast, Gulf of Mexico and Caribbean.

Winds along northern coastline 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/16 to 22 miles per hour) and waves five to seven feet high. Light rains along Sinaloa, Sonora, Nayarit, Jalisco and Michoacan states with wind speeds below 19 km/11 miles per hour along the rest of the coast.

Weak cold front moving west-southwest with strong winds and possible rains along coasts of Tamaulipas, Veracruz, Tabasco and Yucatan peninsula. Winds 15 to 20 knots (28 to 38 km/16 to 22 miles per hour) and waves four to seven feet high.
Hot and partly cloudy with moderate winds from 20 to 30 km per hour.
